## Poster: DarthAnt66 ("Canon and Considerations", CC). It replaces his 2021 "Shedding Limitations" (SL) meta.
Credits for shaping it: KingofBlades, The Ellimist, Azronger, DarthSkywalker0, XSupremeSkillz, Praxis, Beast, Franklin Richards. These people are credited, not posters in the thread.

### I. Canon and assumptions
- Strict "canon truth" can't coexist with debating. Lucasfilm has no power rankings, so the hobby needs starting assumptions.
- Redefine canon truth as "what an optimally rational LFL would think after reviewing ALL sources."
- Legends, as the Story Group treats it, has no hierarchy. Leland Chee says all Legends content (Lego, Infinities, dark-side endings) has equal value, which is no value. So debaters should assume the PRE-2014 Lucasfilm Licensing (LFL) Expanded Universe framework still runs.
- Addendum: building on LFL avoids cherry-picking and gives a shared premise. "Official vs head-canon: the truth always wins."

### II. Canon and officiality
- The LFL EU is beholden to Lucas. Chee quotes cited: "definitely beholden to Lucas' vision", "bound by directives from George Lucas", "would have to bend to fit George's current vision". Essential Reader's Companion: "a story line direct from George Lucas trumps publishing continuity."
- Example: the Visions of the Future novel's Yoda-on-Dagobah Clone Wars references were made non-canon by the ROTS script ("surveys the unfamiliar terrain"), then reconciled by moving them later.
- Two thresholds. Canon1 = official (LFL-published and approved; Chee: "anything that has the LFL copyright" is "official"). Canon2 = continuity (survives the Holocron hierarchy: G > T > C > S; Sue Rostini: "continuous and unified history"; Chee: "the accepted truth of the galaxy").
- Example: most of the Dooku fight in the ROTS novelization is non-canon2 because it contradicts the film, but it is still official.
- S-canon (game stats and mechanics) is "not conclusive"; authors "can use or disregard such material however they saw fit" (Chee).

### III. Canon and power levels (the core claim)
- Nearly all power-level COMMENTARY counts as S-canon in practice. LFL doesn't record power levels in the Holocron, doesn't think they can be "attained or measured", and calls statements "colorful prose for a book" / "for marketing purposes" and stats "for gameplay purposes only". Books should not be "artificially limited." (The reference scans are Chee/LFL replies, imgur, not re-checkable here; one scan is gone per a 2024 note.)
- So "statement binds" ("Wyyrlok is canonically stronger than Nihl because it's stated") is incompatible with LFL. He targets the "Azrongerism" statement-bind meta (2015-16 onward).
- Proposed definition: canon truth = an omniscient LFL ranking from all canon1 sources under the canon2 framework (LFL FACT), then narrowed within ranges of uncertainty by what the actual LFL would rank (LFL INTENT). Fact comes before intent.

### IV. Considerations: weighting the evidence
Every power-level "position" is a weighted point; the verdict is the "point of best fit" across all of them.
Three principles:
- Recency: newer is closer to canon (Chee). "Shedding limitations": a statement has much less weight over characters created after it. Bill Slavicsek on the 2001 Dark Side Sourcebook: "no way we could have included characters that had not yet been created." Sansweet: even the 2008 Complete Encyclopedia only "speak[s] as to the knowledge as of 2008."
- Frequency: how many sources repeat the claim (Chee/WotC interview).
- Visibility: audience size (Chee/WotC). TCW is T-canon partly because of viewership. Obscure leaflets count for less.
Five pillars:
- Coolness: "Which explanation is the coolest?" (Chee/WotC). Example from The Ellimist: Palpatine "easily beaten down by Vaylin" wouldn't happen.
- Officiality: how directly LFL was involved.
- Conformity (starred): in-universe fights, feats and in-universe statements are G/T/C canon, so power readings that keep those events coherent carry MORE weight. Lucas is near-supreme (word of God, including his intent). The ROTS novelization (Stover: "What's in that book is there because Mr. Lucas wanted it to be there") counts as a reflection of Lucas's intent even where it is non-canon2.
- Clarity (starred): the medium distorts things. Sansweet's "every piece... is a window... some windows are a bit foggier." Chee on Force Unleashed: "The Force is definitely amped up to enhance gameplay... What we see in the films are the true representation of Force abilities." Sam Witwer: Lucas "accepted the idea of the Force being amped up to 11... perfect for a game. I don't think he thought it was perfect for the universe." Hidalgo: "Mace isn't as powerful in Episode III as he was in the Clone Wars cartoons." Blurbs are "probably the most unreliable of indicators" (Chee).
- Consistency: how well a claim fits the wider web of claims. Look at the whole picture, not one quote.
LFL intent umbrellas: how it should be, how it's thought to be, how it would be. These lead to authorial intent, theme/narrative fit, fandom perception, source veracity, profitability.

### V. Conclusion (his summary)
- Use the LFL universe, not the "Legends" non-framework.
- Statements are not binding; they're like stats; judge the whole picture.
- Statements especially don't bind characters created after them.
- Weigh consistency, conformity, clarity, recency, frequency, visibility, coolness, officiality.
- Consider LFL intent.

### Primary/official sources cited (quoted in the post, originals not re-checked)
Leland Chee (StarWars.com forums / Holocron posts, WotC interview); Essential Reader's Companion; Star Wars Insider (canon-level explainer); Steve Sansweet, "Ask the Lucasfilm Council" (quoted in full above); Bill Slavicsek (Dark Side Sourcebook); Sam Witwer interview; Pablo Hidalgo (2003 Clone Wars Mace); Matthew Stover on the ROTS novelization; ROTS script (Yoda on Dagobah); Visions of the Future (novel). No character feat scans are cited (the two GIFs are illustrations of the medium point).
Counterarguments/rebuttals: there are no replies in the thread. The SL thread ("Shedding Limitations (Defunct)") is listed as a similar topic.

## Grok's assessment after checking against my notes
AGREE:
- Statements aren't binding trump cards. This matches the user's Oct 11 rule and my own verdicts. For example, I already flag Sidious's "most powerful" accolades as statements and still weigh them heavily but not absolutely (verdicts.md, strongest-character entry).
- Recency/shedding limitations: a 1999 hype line shouldn't cap a character invented in 2008. That directly weakens the "Sith-rank accolades cap Vitiate" flip condition I listed, so I'm keeping the Vitiate #1 lean.
- Conformity: on-page fights and in-universe outcomes have the strongest grounding, because canon has to stay coherent with them. That's why my LotF verdicts lean on the duels (Kavan, the Inferno Ch19 duel) over hype lines.
- Medium clarity: game feats (Force Unleashed, TOR gameplay) are inflated. Use cutscenes and story text, not gameplay.
- Frequency and consistency: one-off claims count for less than repeated ones. I already treat corroborated POV lines (e.g. Caedus admitting Luke beat him in several books) as stronger.
DISAGREE / CAVEATS:
- Statements as "functionally S-canon" goes too far. In-universe statements by reliable characters (e.g. Caedus's own POV "Luke had beaten him", Inferno) are part of the narrative and C-canon, which DarthAnt66 himself concedes under Conformity. Narrator and POV statements in novels are often the AUTHOR telling you who's stronger; that's author intent, not marketing. I keep them as strong evidence. Only out-of-universe hype (blurbs, sourcebook rankings, magazine lines) gets downgraded.
- "Coolness" and "profitability" are too subjective to weigh in a verdict. I'll use them only as tie-breakers.
- Preferring LFL "fact" over intent: I weigh narrative framing and author intent about level with feats rather than strictly second (per the user rule). If a story clearly frames a winner, that matters as much as raw scale.
- "Films are the true power level" would cap all EU feats at film scale. I don't adopt that; EU-internal consistency matters more for Legends-vs-Legends fights.
